reviews.author: Anthony Reyes
reviews.text: Great state park for families with little ones or  folks that are just easing into hiking. Most of the great sights you can get to by vehicle or hike.

reviews.author: Misha Smith
reviews.text:
We recently drove through Moran State Park to check it out for future visits, and it’s absolutely beautiful! The park sits right along the water and is incredibly lush and scenic. While there are no electrical hookups (which means we wouldn’t bring our RV), it’s perfect for tent camping or bringing our truck. We like to scope out parks ahead of time, and this one offers plenty of great sites to choose from, with four different camping areas.

The park also has an awesome spot where you can rent kayaks and canoes, plus a designated swimming area with a beach. There are lots of amenities, and the restrooms were clean and well-kept throughout the park.

A couple of tips: definitely book your campsite well in advance since this is a popular state park, and don’t forget to reserve your ferry tickets to Orcas Island both ways—especially on weekends, as the waits can be long.

We’ll definitely be coming back here for camping and exploring more of what this amazing park has to offer!

reviews.author: Selina Young
reviews.text: The view from the summit is great.  The trail to hike up is a little bit steep. We hiked the cascade falls. It’s easy.

reviews.author: Judy S
reviews.text: Beautiful! Easy access to trails, amenities and a park. Just did the Cascade Lake trail, which is a lovely relatively easy less than 3 mile hike. The views are incredible and terrain varied from forest right down to the lake. There’s a snack shack there, bathrooms and picnic area. Definitely worth the $10 Parking/registration fee.

reviews.author: Carl Berg
reviews.text: Loved this park so many views! So many trails! Yes please! Sunrise or sunset can't go wrong!!! Just during the day it's amazing!

reviews.author: RGL98546
reviews.text: This park is located in a beautiful setting with nice lakeside camp spots and restrooms nearby the campsites with free hot water shower! We enjoyed our stay in the south end campground. There are kayaks for rent on the other side of the lake but we brought our own. A lap around the whole lake , including a little diversion into the lagoon, did not take a huge amount of effort and was very enjoyable. Seeing the seemingly natural bonsai tree on the opposite end of the lake was a nice surprise.  The campground also seemed to be well-staffed. The bathrooms were always clean!
reviews.title: Beautiful, comfortable campground

reviews.author: Companion585201
reviews.text: This park is a gem. It has many hiking trails and the lake is wonderful. The Puget Sound is too cold to swim, but in August this lake is perfect. What a fun day to spend the day in the water, but away from the sea.
reviews.title: Natural gem

reviews.author: Sandywyo
reviews.text: We had a fam reunion Aug 23 at Camp Moran. Wonderful place. Commercial kitchen. Dublexes w comfortable mattresses & bathrooms. We enjoyed hiking trails, waterfalls, mountain lake swimming, cascade lake kayaking & jumping from bridge, Mt constitution.  Swimming /dock area south cascade lake had seaweed and foul odor. We enjoyed swimming elsewhere in the lake and mountain lake was divine. Highly recommend moran state park.
reviews.title: Camp Moran & Moran State Park highly recommend

reviews.text: We did something in Moran State Park every day of our 2 weeks on Orcas Island. I hiked most of the trails, which are varied in scenery and range from easy to difficult. We also biked up to the summit a few times, and that's always exhilarating. We saw bald eagles and a piebald deer during our ascents on the bike. The stand up paddleboarding on Mountain Lake was also just great. Can't wait to get back here.
reviews.title: Fabulous hiking trails, gorgeous views, and fun road bike ride up to the summit

reviews.text: This state park has a wide variety of things to do and scenery to enjoy. I camped here with a bunch of dads and boys in the group camp by Mountain Lake in the middle of the park. There are several camping areas, some by lakes, some in the forest. The sites are spacious and include fire pits and picnic tables. There are no showers by the group camp, but we went swimming in the lake to cool down after our long hike up Mt Constitution, the highest point on Orcas Island (at about 2500ft). The hike up from Mountain Lake rises over 1400ft in about 3.5 miles with a very steep section for the first mile and a gentler climb after that. For those who don't want to work that hard, there is a paved road to the top. At the top, a stone tower rises above the peak to provide outstanding views of the San Juan Islands, Mt Baker, and the valleys, bays, and Cascade Mountain Range on the mainland. The park has many hiking trails (both easy and hard) as well as non-motorized boats on the lakes. The large lake near the entrance has a day-use area with swimming and picnic tables. Moran State Park is several miles from the ferry doc, so you will need a vehicle to really see the park. During the summer, the ferry from Anacortes often fills up and you may end up waiting for the next boat (or two) to get to or from the island, so plan ahead or go during the week when it is less busy. Washington State requires either a day pass or an annual Discover Pass for use of the state parks. You can buy the day pass on site, or stop at a ranger station for an annual or day pass, or go online to order one. The San Juan Islands are very scenic and Orcas Island is a beautiful and popular island to visit. Moran State Park is well worth a visit, whether you just drive through, hike, swim, picnic, or camp there.
reviews.title: Camping at NorthEnd Campground

reviews.text: I understand that most people go to Orcas Island to take a boat tour and view the orcas, but we didn't opt for that. Our friends took us hiking. We went on a lovely hike around Cascade Lake in Moran State Park. It was shaded and beautiful, with views of the lake and forest. We went in the morning and encountered no crowds whatsoever. Mild weather. No bugs. No issues. We found free parking and made a loop that took us about three hours, meandering at a slow pace. There was no fee to enter the area. I am very glad we went here.
reviews.title: Why Sit When You Can Hike?

reviews.text: I live on Orcas Island and go to Moran State Park often. I consider it "The Jewel" of Orcas. Incredible lakes and trails. Great fishing for Rainbow Trout and Large Mouth Bass. This is a large park, over 5000 acres with 5 lakes and an accessible mountain top, Mt Constitution. There's camping, kayak and boat rental on Cascade Lake, I tall stone tower at the top of Mt Constitution, that you can climb for an incredible view all around. Great hiking trails throughout the park, swimming and a small playground. What more could you ask for?
Absolutely stunning state park with amazing mountain hikes, lakes, and views. We visited for the day but many people were camping in the park.

We recently visited Moran State Park for the first time for a weekend, we can't wait to return and stay longer. The only downside was the other campers who stayed up late, we could hear every word they said several camps away! Next time we'll bring some white noise. The tent site was perched on the lake and if we had brought fishing poles, we could have fished from there. We hung up our hammock and it was incredibly beautiful. The bathrooms were clean, and each site had a fire ring/picnic table and waterspout. Not to miss is the trip up to Mt. Constitution. There is a little gift shop and a short hike to the tower and the most amazing views you've ever seen. There is a few tables up there as well, so take a lunch with you. Islands galore. We can't wait to return to fish, rent boats on the lake, take in some of the hikes and other parks around the island. The town is full of local and organic food so not to worry! While waiting for the return trip back to mainland at the ferry, there are several restaurants you can visit while your car is parked in line. We went to the Orca's Hotel restaurant with a great view of the water while we ate. You order at the counter and they will bring it to your table. Very tasty breakfast. Also visit the market right next to the ferry dock, they have a great selection of food and drinks.
reviews.title: Wonderful camping experience

reviews.text: I camped at Moran State Park on Orcas Island during the last week of July 2015. There is so much to do here. Wish I would have had more than the 2 days I stayed. The island itself is beautiful, of course. Lots of hiking options. The hike around Cascade Lake was nice, about 2.5 miles or so. I also hiked up to Sunrise Rock, which is definitely worth the quick elevation gain for the view. I didn't end up hiking all the way up Mount Constitution, but it's possible if you'd like. I did drive up though. Definitely worth checking out the Watchtower and seeing the amazing views from the top. As for the campgrounds, I stayed in the North End campground, which is the first campground you come to inside the park, just before Cascade Lake. That campground wasn't my first choice, but I didn't book my trip early enough to get another site. Book early! North End ended up being pretty nice anyway. I stayed in Campsite 74. Only one bathroom, which was pretty far away from some of the campsites, though (not bad from 74). If I was writing the review solely on the campground itself, I'd probably give it 4 stars, but with everything else accounted for, definitely a 5-star spot that I'll most definitely be back to.
reviews.title: Hike mountain lake

reviews.author: RolandofGilead
reviews.text: Coming from the Midwest it was a nice surprise to find out the island was free of pesky insects like mosquitoes and biting flies. We were there the first week in August the weather was AMAZING! 80 Degrees and blue skies during the day. The water in Cascade Lake and Mountain Lake was perfect. Just cool enough to be refreshing, yet warm enough to stay in all day. Renting a stand up paddle board is a great way to explore the lake and/or lay down and soak up the sun. The hike around the lake is about 3 miles and not too difficult. Plus along the way there are some detours where you can jump off a rock outcropping and then a bridge into the crystal blue water below. The hike around mountain lake is a much wider path and a bit more of a relaxing stroll. Plus there's a rope swing to drop you into the lake when you get too hot. After the rope swing swim the 200 yards to the rock island out in the lake and take in the sights. We loved our time on Orcas and highly recommend Moran State Park.
reviews.title: Dog and kid friendly camping!!

reviews.author: Courtney P.
reviews.text: Even though I grew up on Orcas Island, Moran State Park remains to be my favorite state park in Washington. It offers so many different things from miles of hiking trails to swimming holes, cliffs to jump from, fishing, boating spectacular views and so much more! There are three loops you can choose from; North End, Midway, and South End. Every loop is well kept, and has its own perks. My favorite is the South End due to all of the sites being on the lake with private water access! But you truly can do no wrong with whatever site you end up with! If you have a chance to explore Morans beauty, I highly recommend you do so. Do remember before booking a site that there is an hour long ferry ride to Orcas from Anacortes. You will need reservations in the summer. The camp ground is about 40 minutes drive time from the ferry. No worries though, plenty of sites to see along the way.
reviews.title: What a GEM!!
